title: Azure DNS: public zones, private zones and records

videos.script: Type a name, and an address comes back. It looks like one answer. It is a chain. {{chain}} Each link is a record, in a zone, held by somebody. You will read a whole chain with dig. {{dig}} Azure holds two kinds of zone. A public zone answers the whole internet, but only once the domain is delegated to it. {{delegation}} Delegation means the parent zone points at Azure's four name servers. Until then, the zone answers nobody. {{four}} The top of a zone cannot be an alias. Azure works around that with alias records, which follow a resource's address. {{alias}} A private zone answers only the networks linked to it. Machines can even write their own names into it. {{private}} And the office asks through a resolver in the hub, so its laptops see the same private names. {{resolver}} Three places ask the same question. The lesson is about why each gets the answer it gets. {{end}}
